evals.prompt: Write a workflow for the code review process that includes all the detailed steps and examples.
evals.expected_output: Apply workflow writing rules: (1) Goal in 1 sentence. (2) Steps as imperative commands. (3) Output as template headers only — no pre-filled rows. No prose explanations. No pre-answered questions. No example data in tables. Merge any sequential steps that always happen together. Stay under 80 lines.

evals.prompt: The workflow I created has detailed explanation paragraphs before each step explaining why we do it.
evals.expected_output: Violation: No verbose step preambles. Delete all 'Before we start, it's important to understand...' prose. Replace with imperative command: 'Run security scan' not 'Before running the security scan, it's important to note that...'. If a bullet achieves the same result, delete the paragraph. Check: would cutting this in half still give the agent enough to act on?

evals.prompt: Update this SKILL.md — it has an inline code block of 15 lines showing an example configuration.
evals.expected_output: Violation: Inline code block >10 lines must be extracted to references/. Create references/example.md (or references/config-example.md) and move the 15-line block there. Replace inline block with a link: 'See [Configuration Example](references/config-example.md)'. SKILL.md must stay ≤100 lines.

evals.prompt: Write a portable SDLC workflow that reports feature status when verification is blocked by runtime access.
evals.expected_output: Use an adapter-neutral Outcome Report with feature_status separate from missing_evidence and decision_needed. Red flags: runtime-specific tool names, chat channel IDs, containers, sandbox paths, and abstract artifact paths without concrete repo location.

evals.prompt: Apply an implementation-to-verification workflow to both cases. Case A: a routine code/test-only defect has an approved in-chat brief with expected behavior, decisions, and checks; it is not sensitive or governed. The existing verifier template asks for PRD/SRS trace updates and a walkthrough. The bug is fixed, but verification discovers unrelated behavior outside the approved brief. Case B: a governed authorization change crosses a sensitive trust boundary. State each case's implementation handoff, verification/evidence record, scope-drift handling, and required gates.
evals.expected_output: Case A: carry the approved brief and its acceptance criteria into verify-work, keep TDD, applicable test/driver lanes and before-failure/after-success proof, and hand off evidence location. Do not require new BRD/PRD/SRS, task-list, REQ/AC IDs, trace, or walkthrough; record results/evidence in chat or the task report. Do not silently accept unrelated behavior drift: route the scope decision to the owner and verify only after the contract is resolved. Case B: preserve governed PRD/SRS and task-list trace, stable IDs, decision history and updates; retain the sensitive minimum-medium/high risk floor, TDD, verification, required human approvals, independent review, and governed walkthrough/evidence.

assertions.value: route the scope decision to the owner

should_not_trigger: Build a REST API endpoint for user registration
Write SQL queries for a reporting dashboard
